title: Willingness toward COVID-19 vaccination, coadministration with other vaccines and receive a COVID-19 vaccine booster: a cross-sectional study on the guardians of children in China.
ehr_evidence: The self-administered questionnaire was distributed through the “Xiao Dou Miao” app and 9424 guardians with access to this app participated in the survey that was conducted from September 15 to October 8, 2021.
summary: Cross-sectional survey study investigating changes in guardians' willingness to vaccinate their children against COVID-19, allow coadministration with other vaccines, and receive booster doses, conducted 6 months after a previous survey in China.
key_findings: 86.68% of guardians were willing to vaccinate their children with the COVID-19 vaccine.

Guardians aged 40–49 years (OR=1.54, 95% CI: 1.19–2.00), ≥50 years (OR=2.37, 95% CI: 1.29–4.35), healthcare workers (OR=1.65, 95% CI: 1.17–2.31), and those with children aged ≥3 years (OR=1.50, 95% CI: 1.30–1.73) were more willing.
77% were willing toward coadministration of COVID-19 and influenza vaccines.
64% were willing toward coadministration of other nonimmunization program vaccines.
92% were willing to receive a COVID-19 vaccine booster and 82% were willing to vaccinate their children with a booster.
Higher education and income were associated with lower willingness to vaccinate (e.g., postgraduate education OR=0.40, 95% CI: 0.28–0.58).
captured_features: willingness to vaccinate, coadminister, and receive booster
population: 9424 guardians of children aged <6 years in China
limitations: online questionnaire prevents effective random sampling and limits representativeness
privacy protection prevented longitudinal follow-up of individual respondents
self-reported data may contain information deviation
data_availability_statement: Supplemental data for this article can be accessed on the publisher’s website at https://doi.org/10.1080/21645515.2022.2049169.
